title: List traversal retains the whole list: range/iterate + count/foldl cost ~10µs per cell and grow superlinearly
description:
Measured on master cb1cc36, release build, with and without lib/prelude.blob (cargo xtask prelude-compile): no difference.

- x: range(0, 100000) count — 1.17s; range(0, 400000) count — 4.3s; range(0, 4000000) count — 95s (superlinear: ~24µs/cell).
- eu -S on range(0, 400000) count: 45.2M ticks (~113/cell), 9.6M allocs (~24/cell), 9 collections, Mark 1.38s, Blocks Recycled 0, Peak Blocks 26,937.
- Same shape for iterate(+ 1, 0) take(400000) count (4.27s, 46.4M ticks, Recycled 0) and range(0, 400000) foldl(+, 0) (4.09s, Recycled 0).

Blocks Recycled 0 with peak blocks growing with n suggests the consumed list prefix stays reachable (space leak), so each GC marks an ever larger live set. Possibly also a high per-cell tick and allocation cost. Unknown whether this is a regression (strict range/iterate from eu-oaz72.165, native-in-heap #1247) or long-standing: bisect against 0.15.0 and the bench suite (tests/harness/bench/015..022).

AoC risk: any puzzle walking a few million list cells takes minutes. Found by the AoC 2026 solutions-repository lane.

comments.author: Claude
comments.text:
Diagnosis (interim, measured-single, release build, master cb1cc36, source prelude).
(b) Not a regression from #1247/#1242: binary built at 5aa27b7 (before both) gives the same peak blocks and ticks for range(0,200000) count and the minimal loops below. (#1251 strict-prelude build not completed.)
(a) The consumed prefix IS retained (Recycled 0, peak grows with n, sweep ~0). Retention is the LIST (a CAF-held list of the same length costs MORE blocks than the loop: 16.4k vs 11.8k at n=200k), not the loop frames. Hand-written loops over the same list run in constant space (peak 1,026) unless the loop calls an unknown function parameter: fs(op,l): if(l nil?,0,seq(op(0),fs(op,l tail))) retains; same with op called directly (global add) or no call at all: constant. A counter loop with the same op call does not retain; a list loop that does not call op does not retain. So the trigger is list advance + call of a function-valued parameter (count/foldl-strict call op(i, l head)).
Stack at GC (temporary instrumentation, reverted) shows two Update continuations and a SeqBind persisting for the whole loop, i.e. an in-flight thunk whose env frame can pin its sibling slots (the list-argument thunk, updated in place to the head cons). Not yet proven that this frame is the pin.
Refuted as sole cause: (1) make_arg_array wrapping evaluated cons/native slots in Atom aliases (200k wraps; making them settled removes the wraps, peak unchanged); (2) Global/Value arg atoms capturing caller env; (3) memoising Atom-alias callee slots in enter_local (fires once). 
(c) ~113 ticks/cell: hand-written len loop over take(up) is ~97 ticks/cell, so the tick count is the expected shape for this prelude code; the leak, not ticks, is the superlinear part (mark time grows with live set).

comments.author: Claude
comments.text: Interim handoff: branch eu-oaz72.175/list-retention (docs only) holds docs/superpowers/reports/2026-11-17-list-retention-diagnosis.md and the tracer patch. Tracer on a counter+list loop (d1) shows a frame chain from the running frame via the l parameter = non-update Case closure over the previous frame; but d1 is the lazy-accumulator shape (l demand is Lazy,AtMostOnce), so the tracer must be re-run on range(0,n) count itself. Suspect: update-elided (AtMostOnce) argument closures that are seq-forced and passed on (compiler.rs take_lambda_form / strict_thunk_indices). No fix implemented.
